sets.name: Developer repository size
sets.description: Why the product repository is 35.57 GB. Recommendations only — nothing was remediated.

items.title: HEADLINE: pam/ is 35.57 GB across 28827 files — .git history is 27.88 GB (78.4%) in only 107 files; the working tree is 7.69 GB. The reported 28 GB is the .git folder. Binary artifacts are 98.1% of the packfile; all C# source is 0.8%
items.remediation: See F01-F13

items.title: Three third-party ZIP archives are 73.3% of the repository: ARCONDbeaver.zip (50 versions, 11.45 GiB = 41.1% on its own), multitab.zip (48, 4.589 GiB), dbeaver.zip (36, 4.388 GiB). MEASURED PROOF they cannot compress: 44 of 47 versions in the main pack are stored WHOLE with no delta base. Two of the three are DBeaver, an open-source tool that was never ARCON code
items.remediation: Purge with git filter-repo; distribute via artifact store or release page

items.title: All .zip content is 80.6% of the main packfile from only 262 file versions — the pattern is broader than the three worst offenders
items.remediation: Purge from history plus a server-side pre-receive hook rejecting archives

items.title: Installer packages are committed as source: .msi 1.850 GiB, .exe 1.230 GiB, .deb 0.437 GiB, .pkg 0.211 GiB, .rpm 0.169 GiB on disk. Includes 'ARCON PAM.msi' (7 versions, 0.786 GiB) and dotnetfx.exe, a Microsoft redistributable
items.remediation: Publish to a release/artifact store; purge from history

items.title: .gitignore line 363 declares /PAM — the entire product tree — yet 17872 files under PAM/ are tracked. .gitignore never applies to already-tracked files so the rule is inert AND actively misleading. It would also silently block genuinely new PAM/ files from being staged
items.scope: 17872 tracked files under an ignored path
items.remediation: Remove the false /PAM rule; add real artifact rules; git rm --cached the artifacts

items.title: 3.69 GiB of the checkout is duplicate filenames at different paths, of which 1.51 GiB is byte-identical. NOTE: git stores identical blobs once, so this is a per-checkout cost not history bloat — but it multiplies history as soon as copies drift and are updated separately
items.remediation: Consolidate to one location and reference rather than copy

items.title: msedgedriver.exe is committed at 45 paths with 45 DISTINCT SHAs — 45 genuinely different versions, 593 MB in the checkout alone. chromedriver.exe has 14 copies. Browser drivers are version-pinned downloads, never source
items.remediation: Fetch at test time via WebDriverManager or a CI cache

items.title: PAM/AllSupportingDLLs is 18.02 GiB of LOGICAL history from only 734 file versions — averaging 25 MB per version. A vendored third-party dependency tree under version control. NOTE: logical size; on-disk will be smaller
items.remediation: Migrate to NuGet or an internal package feed

items.title: 3326 remote branches and 307 tags. Every ref keeps its blobs reachable so nothing is ever unreachable — this is why git gc reports zero garbage and the pack never shrinks
items.remediation: Prune merged and abandoned release branches

items.title: Still growing, and one file dominates the growth. A 106-commit pull on 2026-08-10 changing 142 files created a 1.074 GiB pack, of which 0.954 GiB (88.8%) was three NEW versions of ARCONDbeaver.zip — none of which is in HEAD. All C# source in that pull was 0.008 GiB (0.7%)
items.remediation: Fix F04 and F06 first — they are the inflow

items.title: No Git LFS and no .gitattributes anywhere in the repository. The standard mitigation for large binaries was never adopted and nothing constrains binary intake
items.remediation: Adopt Git LFS (see R03) or add a server-side size-gate hook

items.title: A duplicate misnamed 'gitignore' (no leading dot, 6654 bytes) sits beside the real .gitignore (6669 bytes). Git ignores a dotless file entirely; the two differ by 14 lines so rules a developer believes are active are not
items.remediation: Delete gitignore after reconciling its 14 differing lines into .gitignore

items.title: Media and database binaries in source control: 11 .mp4 (43 MB), 5 .db (111 MB including three ~23 MB SQLite files), 2 .bak (25 MB)
items.remediation: Move to shared storage; generate test databases at test time

items.title: Two junk top-level directories are TRACKED (confirmed, 2 files each): '%LOCALAPPDATA%' — a literal unexpanded environment variable used as a folder name by a script that failed to expand it — and '108.0.5359.125' (a Chrome version) whose chromedriver.exe is a 1-BYTE placeholder file
items.remediation: Delete and fix the script that created it

items.title: Generated tooling output was committed on some branch: graphify-out/ (1099 file versions, 0.09 GiB) and a 60 MB syftSbomTable.json. NEITHER is in HEAD — both are reachable from other refs, so they still occupy history
items.remediation: Add to .gitignore; purge in the same history rewrite

items.title: COMPARATOR: the entire QA automation repository is 131 MB total — same organisation, same era, comparable team. This repository is 271x larger
items.remediation: n/a

items.title: ZERO-RISK, AVAILABLE TODAY: make blobless clone the default for every developer and CI job. Since 98.1% of history is binary blobs almost nobody needs, this avoids nearly all of the 27.88 GB transfer while keeping full history
items.remediation: Adopt as the standard clone command

items.title: WILL NOT WORK: git gc / git repack reclaim essentially nothing. count-objects reports loose:0 garbage:0 prune-packable:0 and 3326 refs keep everything reachable. More fundamentally 44 of 47 versions of the largest file are ALREADY stored whole because they cannot be delta-compressed — there is no redundancy left to find
items.remediation: n/a

items.title: FULL RECLAMATION: purging .zip/.msi/.exe/.deb/.rpm/.pkg from all history targets 26.79 GiB -> ~1.3 GiB, a ~95% reduction. This is arithmetic on measured on-disk pack bytes, not a trial run — only a rehearsal on a clone can confirm it
items.remediation: Planned maintenance event with a scheduled freeze

sets.name: Management findings
sets.description: Business-impact framing of the same programme, one row per theme.

items.title: The API has no usable machine-readable contract. 3 of ~6,738 properties are marked required; no length, format or pattern metadata exists; 4 error codes are documented across 1,306 endpoints; 1 of the measured response shapes is documented.
items.impact: Validation depth is capped by documentation, not by test effort. No amount of automation work can assert a rule nobody has written down, so a large fraction of the API can only ever be smoke-tested. Defects in validation logic ship undetected because there is no stated correct behaviour to compare against.
items.remediation: Treat the specification as a deliverable with an owner and a date, not documentation debt. Generate it from the source annotations so it cannot drift, and gate it in CI.

items.title: Only 48 of 1,306 endpoints (3.7%) exist in the PAM developer repository supplied for analysis. The source of the remaining ~96% has not been provided.
items.impact: QA cannot derive request contracts, validation rules or error semantics independently. Every gap becomes a developer question, and the analysis stalls at the speed of those answers.
items.remediation: Confirm which repository and branch build the QA API at u16hf, then either grant read access or commit to publishing the generated spec per build.

items.title: Two ActivityLogs endpoints stop the IIS application pool. Three sequential ordinary requests took the entire API to HTTP 503 with no self-recovery. This was not a load test.
items.impact: A single client making three routine calls can take the product's whole API surface down. LH-08 puts 98 endpoints at risk.
items.remediation: Treat as a production availability defect rather than a test-environment quirk. Automation cannot validate it - re-execution is forbidden - so the fix must be verified by development with the capture in ISSUE-010.

items.title: The shared GenericScheduler service account is locked, and it is simultaneously the automation API account and the data-warehouse ETL account.
items.impact: A test-side lockout became a data-warehouse outage. Automation currently depends on a human manually issuing a 24-hour token before every run, which makes unattended CI execution impossible.
items.remediation: Separate the accounts first - that removes the blast radius immediately - then address the token lifetime. Also unlock GenericScheduler for ETL.

items.title: The framework asserted essentially HTTP status only. Negative testing covered 401/404/405 across 3 controllers; positive testing did not check schema, mandatory fields, business rules, persistence or audit. On an API where rejections return HTTP 200, a status assertion can pass against a rejected request.
items.impact: Green suites were not evidence of correct behaviour. A measured run illustrates the gap precisely: 90% of calls returned HTTP 200 while the true pass rate across all layers was 64%.
items.remediation: Delivered this objective: PamEnvelope, PamApiValidator, ValidationReport, ErrorCodeRegistry, DbPersistenceValidator. Migration of the 71 positive and 5 negative suites is the remaining work and is QA-side, needing no developer dependency.

items.title: Database validation had never run and could not have. AutoConfigs read two DB properties from key names present in no environment file, db_type was hardcoded to mysql while the URL was SQL Server, and DBUtils had zero callers and returned no consumable data.
items.impact: Nothing in the framework ever confirmed that an API-reported write reached the database - the one check that would have caught a Success:true response that wrote nothing.
items.remediation: Replace the supplied sysadmin login with a least-privilege QA-scoped account before persistence checks are wired into CI. See MF-08.

items.title: RESOLVED, and the resolution reverses this finding. It originally claimed the QA API might not write to the supplied database, based on 'no row newer than 2025-10-01 on the server'. That was a sampling error - one column checked in the wrong databases. The newest timestamp in ARCOSDB_U16SP2_WEBSM_QA is 2026-08-03 15:29:18, minutes old, and row counts rose during the investigation. The API's writes land there, confirmed three independent ways: the audit log names created objects in plaintext (runner IP 10.10.1.242, sal_Api_user_id=2), business tables hold them stamped created_by='SYSTEM_API', and ArconPamApiLog holds 194 rows from the runner across 62 methods.
items.impact: Database validation is possible and immediately productive - and it is now the only thing that can settle what the API-side run left open, since for 101 of 107 read-backs the API evidence cannot separate 'never created' from 'created but not readable back'. Column encryption turned out to be narrow (three table families), and the plaintext audit log routes around it.
items.remediation: Retained rather than deleted so the reasoning error and its correction are both traceable. The approach, per-type feasibility and embeddable SQL are in docs/analysis/C-database-validation.md.

items.title: Three security defects found in the QA database during the feasibility study. (1) At-rest encryption is deterministic - one key, no IV, functionally AES-ECB: sso_services holds 20,651 rows but only 59 distinct ss_port ciphertexts, one covering 91% of rows, and an identical ciphertext appears across 3 columns in 2 tables. (2) sso_ApiUsers stores passwords in cleartext, and tbl_KeyEncryptionDecryption holds an unencrypted private key in the same database it protects. (3) 16,560 of 313,197 rows in ssR_Users_Services (5.3%) grant access to services that no longer exist, deletion does not cascade, and only 5 foreign keys exist across 552 tables.
items.impact: In a privileged-access-management product these are the defect classes the product exists to prevent. Deterministic encryption leaks plaintext by frequency analysis with no key at all. Cleartext credentials plus a co-located private key mean read access to the database is read access to everything. Dangling authorisation rows are stale access grants.
items.remediation: Raise separately from the QA findings - these are product security defects, not test observations, and they were found incidentally. Note that fixing the deterministic encryption will break ciphertext-equality lookups, which is why the framework validates by primary key instead and does not depend on the defect.

items.title: The database credential supplied for QA validation is sysadmin and dbcreator on a server hosting 30 databases, several of them not QA, and it is committed in plaintext to the environment file alongside every other credential in all 20 environment files.
items.status: Mitigated in code - account and secret handling outstanding
items.impact: An automated test suite holds unrestricted authority over non-QA data, and the credential is in version control.
items.remediation: Code-level mitigation is already in place - DBUtils refuses non-SELECT statements unless mutation is explicitly enabled, and requests driver-level read-only. That is a guard, not a substitute for correct permissions.

items.title: Chain-dependent testing collapses at the first hop. 196 hops failed to extract a new identifier, and only 2 of 107 created objects could be read back through the API. Only 13 of 217 create endpoints can be driven at all.
items.impact: End-to-end and multi-step workflows - the scenarios that reflect real product use - cannot be automated. Coverage is therefore concentrated on reads, which are the lowest-risk operations.
items.remediation: This is the highest-leverage single unblock available: it converts read-only coverage into genuine lifecycle coverage. It is the same root cause as MF-01 expressed at the execution layer.

items.title: Two latent defects will bite as soon as the suite scales: APIExcelReportUtil mutates a static row index with no synchronisation under parallel='classes', and ApiHelper creates a Playwright instance per request without closing it.
items.impact: Report rows can overwrite each other, and a full-catalogue run leaks resources across 1,300+ requests. Both are harmless at today's test counts and both are directly in the path of the full negative matrix this objective specifies.
items.remediation: Fix before executing any suite over the full endpoint catalogue. Small, self-contained, no developer dependency.

items.title: The bearer token committed to QA_MsSQL.properties expired 2026-07-31, and tokens are valid for 24 hours.
items.impact: Any suite trusting the committed token authenticates as nobody, and its failures will be misread as product defects.
items.remediation: A committed 24-hour credential is wrong on both counts - it is a secret in version control and it is stale within a day. Depends on MF-04 for a durable fix.

items.title: The negative API test suite is largely non-functional, and the functional part tests the opposite of what it claims. 199 of 279 @DataProvider names referenced by the 386 negative test classes do not exist, so 650 @Test methods fail at TestNG initialisation. All 80 providers that do resolve read the POSITIVE data sheets - so a class named MissingParameter submits a complete valid payload. Separately, the 3,652-row negative workbook is declared in AutoConfigs and set in 6 environment files but read by no provider at all.
items.impact: Negative-testing coverage that appears to exist in the repository does not run, and where it runs it asserts the wrong thing. Any past statement of negative coverage based on this suite was not correct.
items.remediation: Triage in three passes - delete what is dead, re-point what is mis-wired, then add assertions using the new validation package. Do not report negative coverage from this suite until pass two is complete. No developer dependency for any of it.

items.title: Evidence now indicates the repository supplied is not merely incomplete but the wrong one. Twelve validation-constraint families return zero occurrences across all 6,866 .cs files, including Newtonsoft's Required.Always - yet the server demonstrably runs that exact check, with 123 rejections of that form observed live. All 3 [Required] attributes in the entire product sit on one class in a Provisioning service that is not among the 70 controllers under test, and their property names appear in 0 of 5,940 endpoint-mapped properties.
items.impact: Sharpens MF-02 from a coverage gap into a sourcing error. The validation logic exists and is running in production; it is simply in code QA has never been given. Time spent analysing pam/PAM for request contracts is time spent on the wrong artifact.
items.remediation: Ask one specific question rather than a general one: which project defines the request models for the ~1,258 endpoints absent from pam/PAM? A single answer unblocks MF-01, MF-09 and most of MF-12's assertion depth.

items.title: 73.4% of a complete negative test design cannot be judged, and 98.7% of endpoints have no runnable negative coverage today. Of 10,448 generated scenarios across all 1,306 endpoints, 7,664 have no documented expected outcome; only 172 (1.6%) carry a measured one. At property level, 98.9% of the derived scenario space is unassertable - 20,469 of 20,700.
items.impact: The negative test design is complete and delivered; what is missing is the product's own statement of correct rejection behaviour. Effort is no longer the constraint - the contract is.
items.remediation: The 7,664 undocumented rows are an itemised, endpoint-level work list ready to hand to development - not a general complaint. Prioritise by controller usage and start with creates.

items.title: The endpoint blocklist that prevents an API outage is enforced in documentation and in the Python harness but NOT in the Java framework the CI pipeline runs. The framework's positive test data holds 102 rows across 50 controllers targeting the blocklisted action names, all expecting HTTP 200. Two of them are the exact endpoints measured to stop the IIS application pool, and they sit in the data for ActivityLogs - the single API class activated by CICD_Suites/APISuite.xml and by a newly git-tracked root testng.xml that IDEs pick up by convention.
items.status: Open - found during OBJ-008, guard not applied pending approval
items.impact: Running the CI API suite, or a developer pressing Run on the project in an IDE, can take the entire QA API to HTTP 503 with no self-recovery. The control that has governed every manual and harness run since the defect was found does not exist inside the framework that actually executes in CI. It is currently protected only by the fact that nobody has run that suite.
items.remediation: Guard on names, never verbs - and put the guard in code rather than in data, because removing the 102 rows leaves nothing to stop them being re-added. This is the clearest case in the project for a safety control living in the framework rather than in a document: the documented rule was followed faithfully for months by everyone who read it, and the one execution path that does not read it is the automated one.

items.title: Some business-name columns are stored encrypted at rest. Encrypted: sso_lobs.sls_name, sso_users.ssu_username, sso_services.ss_username / ss_server_ip / ss_server_host / ss_port (measured examples: 'qxAfNSm6UPULwhCamXOdF
items.status: Mitigated in framework - severity reduced from HIGH on fuller measurement
items.statusDetail: OBJ-007 session, corrected within the same session
items.impact: Affects three table families rather than the whole schema. A lookup by plaintext business name fails on those tables specifically, but the plaintext audit log and the plaintext identity/timestamp columns route around it entirely - so DB validation remains viable.
items.remediation: Validate by integer primary key, which is always plaintext. DbPersistenceValidator.recordExistsById does this; recordExistsByName detects ciphertext in the column and reports INCONCLUSIVE rather than a false negative. For the three encrypted families, the audit log carries the plaintext object name.

items.title: The at-rest encryption is deterministic - the same plaintext yields the same ciphertext everywhere, one key, no IV. sso_services holds 20,651 rows but only 59 distinct ss_port ciphertexts, with one value covering 18,848
items.impact: A security defect in a privileged-access product: deterministic encryption leaks equality and frequency, so an attacker with read access can infer plaintext by frequency analysis without any key. 59 distinct values across 20,651 rows makes the port column effectively readable.
items.remediation: None test-side. Ironically this is also what makes ciphertext-equality lookups work for validation, so a correct fix (randomised IV per row) will break that technique - validate by primary key instead so the test suite does not depend on the defect.

items.title: sso_ApiUsers stores passwords in cleartext (observed pair AUTO40PC47 / <REDACTED>, alongside UsersSecret and UsersKey), and tbl_KeyEncryptionDecryption holds an unencrypted private key in the same database the key prote
items.impact: Anyone with read access to the QA database - which now includes this automation - can read API credentials directly, and can obtain the private key needed to decrypt everything else in the same database. The key being co-located with the data it protects removes the benefit of encrypting the data at all.
items.remediation: None test-side. Reported for immediate escalation. This also raises the stakes on the sysadmin credential issue (OBS-013): read access to this database is read access to credentials.

items.title: 16,560 of 313,197 rows in ssR_Users_Services (5.3%) reference services that no longer exist. Deletion does not cascade, and only 5 foreign keys exist across 552 tables.
items.impact: Dangling authorisation rows in a privileged-access-management product. Rows that grant a user access to a service persist after the service is deleted, and with almost no declared referential integrity the database cannot prevent this class of orphan. If a service identifier is ever reused, a stale grant could resolve against a new service.
items.remediation: None test-side. A data-integrity validation should be added once DB assertions are enabled, since this is exactly the class of defect L11 exists to catch.

items.title: The audit log over-reports creates by roughly 6 to 1 - six 'Created' audit rows for one actual business row.
items.status: Open - documented; framework design avoids the trap
items.impact: The database-side mirror of the Success:true / 'Already Exists' trap: an audit entry is not evidence of a write either. A create assertion must therefore be two-part - the audit row AND the business row - or it will confirm creates that did not happen.
items.remediation: DbPersistenceValidator checks business tables by primary key rather than audit rows. Any audit-based assertion must be paired with a business-table check.

items.title: A CallBack background loop logs errors at a flat rate of about 240 per hour, continuously, before during and after any test activity. It inflated the run window's apparent error count from 194 to 1,736.
items.impact: Nine tenths of the errors in the run window were not test-caused. Any error-rate metric taken from this environment without excluding the CallBack loop is wrong by roughly an order of magnitude - and would have been misattributed to the test run.
items.remediation: Exclude the CallBack loop by predicate when measuring error rates. Fix the loop itself - it is a product defect independent of testing.

items.title: Only 2 of the 6 object creations in the 2026-07-29 run window were attributable to the test - the environment has concurrent activity. A bare COUNT(*) delta across a test window is therefore unsafe.
items.impact: Any DB assertion built on counting rows before and after will produce false positives from other users' activity. Every count needs an attribution predicate (created_by = 'SYSTEM_API', the runner IP, or the API user id).
items.remediation: DbPersistenceValidator asserts on a specific primary key returned by the API rather than on counts, which sidesteps this entirely. Where a count is unavoidable, add an attribution predicate.

items.title: AutoConfigs read the DB configuration from property keys that exist in no environment file: db_name read 'databaseName' and db_user_name read 'db_user', while the environment files declared db_name and db_user_name.
items.impact: Both fields resolved to null even in a fully populated environment, so a DB connection could never have been opened. This is the mechanical reason no DB assertion has ever run in this framework.
items.remediation: None needed - fixed. AutoConfigs.dbProperty() now reads the canonical key and falls back to the historic one, so environment files written against either spelling work. Upstream had independently populated QA_MsSQL.properties using the historic spellings, which the fallback covers.

items.title: AutoConfigs.db_type was the hardcoded literal "mysql" while DBUtils built a jdbc:sqlserver URL and logged 'Connecting to MSSQL'. Three different databases were described in one code path.
items.impact: Any logic branching on db_type would have taken the MySQL path against a SQL Server target. The pom still declares mysql-connector-j 9.0.0 alongside mssql-jdbc 12.8.0.
items.remediation: None needed - fixed. db_type is now read from the environment and defaults to mssql.

items.title: DBUtils had zero callers anywhere in the framework, and every method returned void or printed to System.out. executQuerry returned a ResultSet over a connection that getConnection() had already opened separately and getO
items.impact: No test in the framework performed any database validation. The utility was unusable for assertion, not merely unused.
items.remediation: None needed - rewritten. query() returns fully materialised rows and closes the connection before returning; count(), exists(), queryScalar() and queryFirstRow() are assertion-shaped.

items.title: The bearer token committed into Environments/QA_MsSQL.properties as ApiToken expired 2026-07-31 10:39 UTC (JWT nbf 2026-07-30 10:39, exp 2026-07-31 10:39 - a 24-hour token).
items.impact: Any suite relying on the committed token authenticates as nobody. Combined with the locked GenericScheduler account, there is no self-service path to a working token.
items.remediation: Owner supplies a fresh token via $env:PAM_API_TOKEN per run. Never retry /arcontoken - the account locks harder.

items.title: POST /arcontoken returns HTTP 400 {"error":"Your account has been locked. Please contact your supervisor"}. The locked GenericScheduler account is also the data-warehouse ETL service account.
items.impact: The lockout reaches past testing into the ETL pipeline. A single shared service account for both automation and ETL means a test-side lockout is a production-side outage.
items.remediation: Manually issued token, one per run. Longer term the automation needs its own dedicated, non-shared service account.

items.title: GET /api/ActivityLogs/GetErrorLogs and GET /api/ActivityLogs/GetLogs each hang for 30 s and stop the IIS application pool. Three sequential requests took the whole API to HTTP 503 with no recovery without intervention. T
items.impact: Three ordinary requests constitute a denial of service against the entire API surface. LH-08 puts 98 endpoints at risk.
items.remediation: Hard blocklist enforced at planning time, before a request is built. GetAllActiveUserDetails is blocklisted for the same reason. Live re-validation is forbidden, not merely skipped.

items.title: A rejected request normally returns HTTP 200 with the rejection in the response body. Five distinct response-envelope shapes were measured on this one API, and the payload documentation describes one of them.
items.impact: An assertion on status alone passes against a fully rejected request. An assertion written to a fixed envelope shape fails on correct responses from endpoints with a different shape - so a generic assertion cannot be written without normalisation.
items.remediation: New com.arcon.utils.validation.PamEnvelope normalises all observed shapes - envelope with array/object/absent Result, bare array, error form, and both field casings - behind one accessor set.

items.title: POST /api/ServiceCreation/SetServiceDetails returns Success:true with Message:'Already Exists' when the record already exists. Nothing is inserted; both the status code and the Success flag are green.
items.impact: Success:true is not evidence of a write. A create assertion built on status plus flag reports a pass for an operation that wrote nothing - the framework would have counted a no-op as a successful create.
items.remediation: PamApiValidator.expectInserted() asserts Message semantics and explicitly fails 'Already Exists', naming the green status and flag in the failure message so the cause is unmistakable.

items.title: ApiHelper hardcoded KNOWN_ERROR_CODES = {201,202,203} and failed any test whose response carried an error code outside that set. A live run captured ErrorCode '206-LC_GLD' on HTTP 200 from POST /api/Logs/GetLogDetails -
items.impact: The framework could not distinguish 'unexpected error code' from 'error code nobody documented'. Because no product error-code registry exists (4 codes documented for 1,306 endpoints), that distinction is unavailable in principle, not just in practice.
items.remediation: New ErrorCodeRegistry matches on the numeric prefix, includes 206, and records an unknown code as an observation rather than a failure - the defect is the missing registry, not the response.

items.title: A superseded copy of validateResponseErrorCode and its caller sits commented out immediately above the live definitions in ApiHelper (roughly lines 1282-1394; the live ones follow at 1397 and 1464). A grep for the method
items.impact: Any reader - human or tool - reasoning about envelope validation from a grep reaches the wrong code. It has already been necessary to warn about this in the workspace guidance.
items.remediation: Check for a leading // before concluding anything about behaviour. The dead block should simply be deleted; git history preserves it.

items.title: WITHDRAWN - this observation as first written was wrong, and is corrected here rather than deleted. It claimed 'no row newer than 2025-10-01 exists on that server, while the API run executed 2026-07-29', and inferred tha
items.status: Withdrawn - corrected by OBS-045 within the same session
items.statusDetail: OBJ-007 session, withdrawn by OBJ-007 session
items.impact: The correction is materially good news and reverses the conclusion: the QA API's writes DO land in ARCOSDB_U16SP2_WEBSM_QA, confirmed three independent ways - the audit log names the created objects in plaintext (AUTO40PC47, runner IP 10.10.1.242, sal_Api_user_id=2), business tables hold them stamped created_by='SYSTEM_API' (ssu_id=1457, ss_service_id=25342, sso_ApiUsers RowId=365), and ArconPamApiLog holds 194 rows from the runner across 62 methods. DB validation is therefore possible and immediately productive. See OBS-045.
items.remediation: Not applicable - withdrawn. Retained so the reasoning error is visible and the corrected conclusion is traceable.

items.title: Database validation is POSSIBLE against ARCOSDB_U16SP2_WEBSM_QA and the API's writes demonstrably land there. Feasibility per type: record creation possible; update possible (sal_old_value to sal_new_value in the audit l
items.status: Delivered - approach documented, blocked on the account change
items.impact: This is the single most valuable outcome of the objective's DB item, because DB validation is now the ONLY thing that can settle what the API-side run left open - for 101 of 107 read-backs the API evidence cannot separate 'never created' from 'created but not readable back'.
items.remediation: One blocker before switching it on: the configured login is sysadmin (OBS-013). Least-privilege DDL is provided in docs/analysis/C-database-validation.md section 6.1.

items.title: The database independently corroborates the API-side root-cause split. Sweeping all 177 populated tables carrying a creation timestamp, the entire 3h20m run window gained only 110 rows - 94 of them logging side-effects a
items.impact: Exactly what 'most creates never happened' predicts (117 of 196 creates genuinely failed). Two independent methods - API response analysis and a full-schema database sweep - reach the same conclusion, which is the strongest form of evidence available here and makes the finding safe to escalate.
items.remediation: Not applicable - this is corroboration, not a defect.

items.title: The supplied devops login is sysadmin and dbcreator on a server hosting 30 databases, several of which are not QA (ARCOSDB, MOF_Dwh_Raw, ARCOSRDPDB_icici, OnboardingDB).
items.status: Mitigated in framework - account change recommended
items.impact: An automated suite holding sysadmin over non-QA data is an unbounded blast radius. A single mistaken statement is unrecoverable, and the credential is committed in plaintext into the environment file.
items.remediation: Read-only discipline is enforced in code: DBUtils refuses any non-SELECT statement unless allowMutations() is called explicitly, and requests connection-level read-only from the driver (accepted by the SQL Server driver, verified). A least-privilege account scoped to the QA database with SELECT only should replace it.

items.title: System JAVA_HOME points at C:\Program Files\Java\jdk-26.0.1, which does not exist, and the java on PATH is 26.x while pom.xml requires Java 21. Maven fails until JAVA_HOME is overridden per session.
items.impact: Every session begins with a build that cannot run. New joiners hit it before doing any work.
items.remediation: $env:JAVA_HOME = 'C:\Program Files\Eclipse Adoptium\jdk-21.0.11.10-hotspot' before any mvn invocation. mvn resolves on the PowerShell PATH only, not in Bash.

items.title: APIExcelReportUtil increments a static int rowIndex with no synchronisation while API suites run parallel='classes'. ApiHelper additionally calls Playwright.create() per request and never closes the instances.
items.impact: Rows can overwrite each other in Api_Report.xlsx, and at 1,300+ requests the unclosed Playwright instances are a real resource leak. Both are latent at today's test counts and bite exactly when the suite is scaled to the full endpoint catalogue - which is what this objective's negative matrix implies.
items.remediation: None applied this session - out of scope for OBJ-007's stated items. Must be fixed before executing a full-catalogue suite.

items.title: Upstream committed graphify-out/ to origin/Dev, including a 748,669-line graph.json, which collided with the locally generated untracked graphify-out/ and aborted the merge.
items.impact: A 150 MB regenerable build artifact is now in git history, and any developer with a locally built graph cannot merge without moving it aside first.
items.remediation: The local graph was moved to 'Automation gitlab repo/graphify-out.local-backup-OBJ007' (outside the repo, so it creates no git noise) and the merge then fast-forwarded cleanly. graphify-out/ should be gitignored and the committed copy removed.

items.title: ApiHelper.validateResponseErrorCode read node.has("success") in camelCase, and Jackson is case-sensitive. A census of all 1,868 captured responses found lowercase 'success' in 0 of them and PascalCase 'Success' in 1,580.
items.impact: The framework's only application-envelope assertion could never pass. Every negative case that reached it failed with 'Response body missing success field' - a wrong reason, meaning the layer had zero real coverage while appearing to exist. Any green run predating this fix proves nothing about envelope behaviour.
items.remediation: None needed - fixed. Field access now delegates to PamEnvelope, which resolves either casing, unwraps a single-element array only when it genuinely is an envelope, and classifies the shape.

items.title: 31 distinct top-level response shapes were measured across the 1,868 captured calls. Only 6 match a documented shape; 25 do not. 127 calls are not JSON objects at all, 288 carry no Success field, 139 of 1,291 Result valu
items.impact: Far worse than the 4-5 shapes previously recorded. No generic assertion can be written against this API without a normalisation layer, and no consumer can write a single deserialisation model.
items.remediation: PamEnvelope classifies into 8 shape classes, all 8 of which occur in the evidence. Root CLAUDE.md corrected from 'four envelope shapes' to the measured 31.

items.title: 70 instances were measured where Success:true accompanied no write. Breakdown: 6 'Already Exists', 4 success-carrying-a-validation-error, 1 bare false, 48 success-with-no-data, 11 silent writes. The 'Already Exists' stri
items.impact: The framework catches 0 of the 70. The harness's L1-L7 caught 14, so 56 passed every layer that ran. Any create assertion built on status plus flag is unsound, and because the message text varies, classification must be pattern-based rather than a literal match or a per-endpoint allowlist.
items.remediation: PamApiValidator.expectInserted() matches on message semantics with substring patterns ('insert' present and 'already exist' absent) rather than exact strings.

items.title: APIConfig.java yields 1,308 distinct Controller/Action pairs against the canonical 1,306. The two extras are AzureKeyVault/GetDatabaseStatus - a real endpoint dropped from the count by a double-slash typo at APIConfig.ja
items.impact: A real endpoint is silently uncounted and therefore untested. The canonical 1,306 remains correct to quote, but the catalogue itself carries two defects.
items.remediation: Not corrected this session - changing the count would invalidate cross-references in every existing report. Fix the typo and the count together, deliberately.

items.title: Three independent wiring gaps: 7 data providers point at Excel tables that do not exist (UAG*, UserDiscovery, Kotak) so those tests cannot run at all; 9 of 79 positive test classes are referenced by no suite XML; and 210
items.impact: Tests that appear to exist cannot execute, classes that exist are never scheduled, and a 210-endpoint slice of the surface is driven from Excel without a catalogue entry. Coverage counted from any single source is wrong.
items.remediation: None applied - reported for the owner to triage. Each is small and independently fixable.

items.title: 97 of the 107 L6 read-back checks could not have passed under any circumstances. chain_runner.store() refuses a None, so NEW_ID never entered vars; substitute() then returned the placeholder token unchanged (chain_runner
items.status: Open - harness fix outstanding; framework already models it correctly
items.impact: The headline '105 of 107 read-backs failed' is largely a harness artifact, not product evidence. Those 97 verdicts carry no information about persistence at all. Reporting them as product failures would have been wrong, and any escalation built on that number would have been indefensible.
items.remediation: Harness fix required in chain_runner.py: skip the L6 check when the placeholder is unresolved and record NOT RUN rather than FAIL. The framework equivalent is already correct - ValidationOutcome distinguishes NOT_RUN from FAIL precisely so this class of error cannot recur.

items.title: Of the 10 L6 checks that searched for a real value, 2 verified, 2 are harness false negatives (the read-back answered 'Record Already Exists.' - positive evidence of existence, recorded as FAIL), 4 never queried the stor
items.impact: For 101 of 107 hops the run cannot separate 'never created' from 'created but not readable back' - the distinguishing observation was never made. Only a read-only SELECT against ARCOSDB_U16SP2_WEBSM_QA can settle it, which is exactly what makes the DB write-target question (OBS-012) blocking rather than incidental.
items.remediation: Treat the L6 figures as inconclusive pending DB confirmation. Tighten identifier extraction to reject non-identifier field types.

items.title: Root-cause split of the 196 MISSING ['NEW_ID'] chaining failures: 117 the create genuinely failed and no identifier ever existed (26 non-200, 89 HTTP 200 with Success:false, 2 non-standard error payloads); 19 the create
items.impact: The harness is not at fault - cause (c) is zero, evidenced by two searches far wider than the extractor (every dict to 12 levels, and any key matching id|code|key|guid|ref|no|num|seq|sr) finding zero hits across all 196 responses. Widening the extractor would recover none of them. The 19 acknowledged-but-no-identifier cases are a genuine API design defect: a create that returns no handle to what it created cannot be chained by anyone, including a real client.
items.remediation: None available test-side. The 19 need the API to return the created identifier; the 117 need valid request bodies (OBS-017).

items.title: A second typo in APIConfig.java: 'Se0rviceDetailsV3' (a zero for an 'e'), which produces a hard 404 at runtime. This is distinct from the double-slash typo at APIConfig.java:188 recorded in OBS-021.
items.impact: A declared endpoint constant can never resolve, so whatever it was meant to cover is untested and the failure looks like a product 404 rather than a catalogue error.
items.remediation: Both catalogue typos should be corrected together, deliberately, since fixing them changes the canonical endpoint count that existing reports cross-reference.

items.title: Only 2 of 326 flows achieved a real multi-hop chain - user_lifecycle and service_lifecycle - and both were hand-written with pinned extract selectors. The depth cliff is at hop 4 to hop 5: 131 flows (40%) died at the cre
items.impact: Auto-generated chaining does not currently work beyond the create boundary. The two successes prove the mechanism is sound when the create returns a usable identifier - so the blocker is the API contract and the payload gap, not the generator design.
items.remediation: Hand-pin extract selectors for high-value lifecycles as an interim measure, which is what the two working flows do.

items.title: 199 of the 279 @DataProvider names referenced by the 386 negative test classes do not exist, so 650 @Test methods fail at TestNG initialisation. Of the 80 providers that do resolve, all read the POSITIVE sheets - so for
items.impact: The negative test suite is largely non-functional, and the part that does run tests the opposite of what its name claims. A test called MissingParameter that submits a complete valid payload will pass while asserting nothing about missing parameters. This is worse than absent coverage because it reads as coverage.
items.remediation: None applied - the scale of rewiring is beyond this objective's stated items and needs owner triage. Every negative class must be re-pointed at negative data before any negative figure from this suite can be trusted.

items.title: The 3,652-row negative Excel workbook is loaded by nothing. AutoConfigs.java:37 declares Negative_API_ExcelDataProviderFileName and 6 environment files set it, but no data provider reads it. 3,049 rows are unreachable, a
items.impact: Substantial authored test data has never executed. The declared-but-unread property gives every appearance of being wired up, which is why this went unnoticed.
items.remediation: None applied. Either wire a provider to the negative workbook or remove the property and the workbook, but do not leave it declared and unread.

items.title: Of 10,448 generated negative scenarios across all 1,306 endpoints, 7,664 (73.4%) have no documented expected outcome at all. Only 172 (1.6%) carry a measured expected outcome; 2,612 (25%) can rely on a framework-asserted
items.impact: Three quarters of a complete negative test design cannot be asserted, because nobody has documented what a rejection should look like. This quantifies precisely what the missing contract costs: the tests can be designed but not judged.
items.remediation: Rows are marked 'UNKNOWN - contract undocumented' rather than given a plausible guess, so the gap is countable and can be handed to development as a specific list.

items.title: The endpoint count reconciles exactly, and the origin of the stale figures is now established: APIConfig.java holds 1,322 raw route constants; removing 13 surplus (11 paths declared by more than one constant) gives 1,309
items.impact: Settles a recurring source of confusion. 1,322 is the raw constant count and 1,306 is the endpoint count - both are correct answers to different questions, which is why both circulated.
items.remediation: Quote 1,306 for endpoints and say 'route constants' when quoting 1,322. Recorded here so the distinction is not lost again.

items.title: Independent confirmation of LH-08 by catalogue counting: GetLogs plus GetErrorLogs appear across exactly 98 endpoints. The full execution blocklist is 110 endpoints marked DO NOT EXECUTE - takes API down (14 named explic
items.impact: Confirms the 98-endpoint figure from an entirely independent method. 160 endpoints (12% of the surface) cannot be safely executed by automation as the product currently stands.
items.remediation: Blocklist enforced at planning time. Guard on endpoint names, never verbs - deletion is POST /api/<Controller>/Delete<Thing>.

items.title: The new validation layer is verified against real captured responses rather than invented fixtures. PamValidationLayerTest runs 15 tests over bodies taken from artifacts/runs/2026-07-29_181439/evidence, covering all 8 Pa
items.impact: Gives the framework change evidential standing: it demonstrably handles the shapes this API actually produces, and it makes no network or database calls, so it runs anywhere without a token and cannot trip the blocklist.
items.remediation: Not applicable - this is the verification, not a defect.

items.title: The 3-of-6,738 claim reproduces exactly (6,866 .cs files, 6,738 auto-properties, 3 [Required], 0.0445%), but the denominator is the wrong population. All three [Required] attributes sit on one class - ProvisioningService
items.impact: On the API surface actually under test the declared-required count is 0 of 5,175, not 3 of 6,738. The finding is therefore stronger than stated, not weaker: there is no declared mandatory-field metadata at all for anything being tested.
items.remediation: Quote both figures with their scope attached. Corroborated from a third direction: 102 of 102 archived Swagger-validated operations record 'schema declares no required properties'.

items.title: Twelve constraint families return zero occurrences across pam/PAM, including all of [StringLength], [MaxLength], [MinLength], [Range], [RegularExpression] and Newtonsoft's Required = Required.Always. Yet the server demon
items.impact: Decisive evidence that the models enforcing validation are not in the repository supplied. The absence of the attributes is not evidence that validation does not exist; it is evidence that the code implementing it was not provided. That reframes the developer-repo gap from 'incomplete' to 'the wrong repository'.
items.remediation: None test-side. Development must identify where the enforcing request models live.

items.title: 185 of 217 create endpoints (85.3%) have no mandatory-field signal of any kind, and 66 have no known properties at all. Only 32 (14.7%) have any metadata, and 29 of those were recovered from rejection prose rather than a
items.impact: A create payload cannot be constructed from any documented source for 85% of create endpoints. Worse, the metadata gap also removes the means of diagnosis: of 213 creates called, the server named a missing property in 31 cases and stated no cause in 150.
items.remediation: Rejection-prose mining recovered metadata for 29 endpoints - a genuine but fragile source, since the grammar and field naming both vary.

items.title: 98.9% of the derived property-level negative scenario space is unassertable - 20,469 of 20,700. By class: missing-mandatory 4,951 unassertable against only 224 authorable; max-length 5,175; format 5,175; pattern/enum 5,1
items.impact: Quantifies exactly what the missing contract costs: the negative tests can be designed but not judged. The existing corpus overwhelmingly tests the transport layer rather than the product's own validation.
items.remediation: None. This is the direct, measured consequence of OBS-034 and OBS-036.

items.title: Two distinct findings about the negative Excel corpus. (1) The ExpectedErrorCode column is absent from all header blocks - the column does not exist, which is stronger than the previously reported 'zero rows populated'.
items.status: Open - (2) is a definitional gap, not an arithmetic error
items.impact: On (1): the framework cannot assert an application-level error code from Excel-driven negative data because there is nowhere to put the expectation. On (2): the important point is that NO CONCLUSION DEPENDS ON THE TOTAL - the 405/401/200 split re-derives identically at 1,604/1,550/13, and only 13 rows target application validation, under every counting rule. Quoting a bare total is the error; quoting the split is safe.
items.remediation: Add the ExpectedErrorCode column, then populate it as the error-code registry becomes available. For the count: agree ONE definition and put it in the counting script rather than in prose. Until then, quote the 405/401/200 split and the 13 application-validation rows - the figures that are stable - and give any total with its counting rule attached. Do not declare a sixth 'settled' number.

items.title: The endpoint blocklist is enforced in the documentation and in the Python harness but NOT in the Java framework's test data. testdata/API_Automation_Test_Input_Data.xls sheet AllApiPositiveScenarios contains 102 rows acr
items.status: Open - reported, awaiting a decision on the guard
items.impact: CRITICAL and live. Running the CI API suite - or opening the project in an IDE, which picks up a root testng.xml by convention - drives the two endpoints that took the whole API to HTTP 503 after three sequential calls with no self-recovery. The safety rule that has governed every manual and harness run since it was discovered has no equivalent inside the framework the CI pipeline actually executes. It is protected today only by the fact that nobody has run that suite.
items.remediation: Not applied - a framework change is outside OBJ-008's stated scope and OBJ-007's work is still uncommitted awaiting review, so adding more would muddy that review. Recommended fix is a name-based guard in ApiHelper that refuses a request whose action name is blocklisted, failing the test with a clear message rather than issuing the call - guarding on names, never verbs. Removing the 102 rows is the alternative but is fragile, since nothing then stops them being re-added.

items.title: A root testng.xml now exists and is git-tracked, having arrived in the upstream Dev merge (commit 4a40b81). It runs one class - ActivityLogs - and carries no <listeners> block. Both AGENTS.md section TestNG suites and th
items.status: Open - documents corrected under OBJ-008; the file itself left in place
items.impact: Two consequences. IDEs pick up a root testng.xml by convention, so this is a plausible accidental route into OBS-047 - a developer pressing Run on the project could drive the app-pool-killing endpoints without ever opening a suite file. And with no listeners registered, TestListener never runs, so APIExcelReportUtil is never initialised and no Excel report is produced - the same trap as -Dtest.
items.remediation: Correct both documents. Either delete the root testng.xml or give it listeners and a safe class; leaving an undocumented, listener-less root suite pointing at the most dangerous class in the catalogue is the worst of the options.

items.title: Data-corruption and naming defects in testdata/API_Automation_Test_Input_Data.xls sheet AllApiPositiveScenarios: row 1418 holds the mangled path 'ck/api/Us/nv/gg/bnerLabels/GetErrorLogs' instead of '/api/UserLabels/GetEr
items.impact: A corrupted path produces a 404 that reads as a product defect rather than a data defect - exactly the confusion that wastes investigation cycles. Mismatched controller names break any coverage measurement that joins the Excel corpus to APIConfig.java by controller.
items.remediation: None applied. A validation pass over the workbook - every path parses, every controller name resolves against APIConfig.java - would catch this class of defect and should run in CI.

items.title: Four figures in workspace documents have drifted from measurement, found while authoring the knowledge base: the database count is 31 by sys.databases while OBS-013 and MF-08 say 30; source files under src/test/java are
items.impact: Individually minor, collectively the pattern that produced the '54 of 70' error - a figure written once, inherited as fact, and never re-measured. The last two are my own drafting errors: I wrote report B before the database findings landed and did not revisit it.
items.remediation: All four corrected under OBJ-008. The durable fix is the knowledge base itself: a figure with a cited basis can be re-checked, which is why every row requires evidence.

items.title: Mandatory-field metadata is effectively unavailable: 3 properties of roughly 6,738 carry a Required marker, and there is no length, format or pattern validation metadata anywhere in the supplied sources.
items.impact: A generated create payload cannot be known-valid, so a create cannot be reliably driven; a failed create returns no identifier; without an identifier a chain cannot proceed past its first hop. It also makes an honest 'missing mandatory field' negative test impossible to author, because which field is mandatory is unknown.
items.remediation: PamApiValidator records L9_MANDATORY_FIELDS as NOT_RUN with an explicit reason when no mandatory set is supplied, so the gap is visible in every report instead of being absorbed as a pass.
